bog_iron.name: Bog-iron
bog_iron.desc: A lump of iron raked from the fen and hammered once. A smith can fold it into an edge.

gourd.name: Gourd
gourd.desc: A stoppered gourd of hot broth. Rest at a Hearthstone and it is full again. Somebody has cut a small notch in the neck for every time it has been refilled, and then given up.

arrows.name: Arrows
arrows.desc: Goose-fletched arrows for the bow. Carried in the quiver, not the hand.

deep_gourd.name: Deep Gourd
deep_gourd.desc: A larger gourd. Holds one more draught.

mend.name: Mending Song
mend.desc: A low hum sung over cuts and chilblains, mostly to children, until they stop crying out of embarrassment. Every household on the coast sings it slightly differently. Ingra sings it flat and says that is how it goes.

ember_throw.name: Ember Throw
ember_throw.desc: A coal of remembered summer, thrown. It goes where the breath is aimed.

hearth_shout.name: Hearth Shout
hearth_shout.desc: The whole hearth at once. Everything near learns what midsummer felt like.

long_note.name: Long Note
long_note.desc: One held note driven straight through everything between you and the far wall.

warding_hum.name: Warding Hum
warding_hum.desc: A skin of remembered warmth that takes the cold's anger first, and goes out doing it.

armour_traveller_coat.name: Traveller's Coat
armour_traveller_coat.desc: A long coat of grey southern wool, wrong for the north, warm enough on a boat. The toggles are horn. One is a replacement and does not match.

armour_saltfell_oilskins.name: Saltfell Oilskins
armour_saltfell_oilskins.desc: Brede's spare oilskin smock, dressed with fish oil and smelling of it. It turns sea-spray and some of the cold. The left cuff has been let down and re-hemmed by someone who did it properly.

saltfell_shield.name: Saltfell Board Shield
saltfell_shield.desc: A round shield of pine boards with a bog-iron boss, painted woad blue long ago. It hung over the boat-shed door and was used mostly to keep the rain off the door.

fostering_horn.name: Fostering Horn
fostering_horn.desc: A cow's horn with a soapstone stopper and a draught-hole, worn at the hip. Children of Saltfell carry a coal from the home hearth in one when they are sent down the water. The coal inside has been fed every evening since you were small.

desc_when.desc: A cow's horn with a soapstone stopper and a draught-hole, worn at the hip. It is empty. The inside is black to the lip.
The horn a child carries down the water. The coal inside has been fed for twenty years. It was given with an instruction, and the instruction was followed.

item_net_float.name: Brede's Net-Float
item_net_float.desc: A cork float off a herring net, with Brede's knot burned on one side. He burned a second knot on the other side the year they married, got it wrong, and never burned a third.

ks_child_mask.name: Child's Mask
ks_child_mask.desc: A small mourning mask of birch with a woad-blue band, hung on the low peg by the Longhouse door. Children are given one to grow into. The band has been retied to fit a smaller head.

ks_knucklebones.name: Knucklebones
ks_knucklebones.desc: Four sheep's knucklebones, the fifth missing, worn smooth in a small pocket. The game is to throw one up and snatch the rest before it lands. One of them has a tooth-mark.

item_rye_sack.name: Rye Sack
item_rye_sack.desc: A sack of rye from the Saltfell store-house, chewed at one corner. It was under the byre dog, flattened into the shape of a dog. Ingra will want it back.

item_mending_needle.name: Mending Needle
item_mending_needle.desc: A net-needle of whalebone, loaded with tarred twine, from the Netmender's lap. The last net it worked has one hole mended fourteen times over. Each knot is a little looser than the one before it.

item_tally_stick.name: Arne's Tally-Stick
item_tally_stick.desc: A long hazel stick from Arne Holm's belt, notched down both edges, one notch for every barrow he turfed over on the coast. He could tell you whose each notch was. The last two sit side by side, and both are cut only halfway.

item_twin_spindles.name: The Twins' Spindles
item_twin_spindles.desc: Two drop-spindles of birch with soapstone whorls, tied together with a bit of yarn. One shaft is grey from handling and its whorl is worn smooth. The other still has the knife marks on it.

item_orm_cord.name: Orm's Knot-Cord
item_orm_cord.desc: A barrow-keeper's cord as long as two arms, with a knot for every burial on the Kin-Mounds in the order of the mounds. Orm tied his knots tight and small. The last knot on the cord is looser, and a different knot.

item_hesk_tongs.name: Hesk's Tongs
item_hesk_tongs.desc: Smith's tongs of bog-iron with long reins, one rein bent from being used as a lever. Hesk has punched his mark into both reins, in case anyone on the Lowe was thinking of keeping them.

ks_woad_thread.name: Woad Thread
ks_woad_thread.desc: A length of woad-blue wool tied round a flat stone on the turf of a closed barrow. It is knotted with a household knot, pulled tight with the teeth. The wool is still soft.

turf_song.name: Turf-Laying Song
turf_song.desc: Sung by barrow-keepers while the turf goes back, to keep the spades together. Most of it is counting. Aud gets the numbers in the wrong order and finishes on the right one.

armour_barrow_cloak.name: Orm's Working Cloak
armour_barrow_cloak.desc: A cloak of fulled brown wool pinned at the right shoulder, worn for cutting turf in the rain. Orm was long in the arm, and Aud never took the sleeves up. The hem is still stiff with Lowe mud.

item_ivo_mitten.name: Ivo's Mitten
item_ivo_mitten.desc: A child's mitten of felted grey wool with a leather palm, the thumb darned in a different grey. It was frozen into the new ice over the hole, palm up. The darn is his grandfather's; the stitches are too big.

item_kettle_ladle.name: Kettle Ladle
item_kettle_ladle.desc: An iron ladle as long as an arm, for the fish-kettles, with a hook at the end to hang it on the pot. It was standing upright in a pot of supper on the hook in the end house. The fire under the pot had been banked up and banked up again.

item_halla_cord.name: Halla's Knot-Cord
item_halla_cord.desc: A trader's cargo cord, tarred, a knot for every barrel and bale and passenger, in the trader's own tight hand. The last knot is tied loose, by someone who knew the knots but not well. It says one man, sick.

armour_icefur.name: Ice-Fur Coat
armour_icefur.desc: A coat of grey sheepskin worn fleece-in, with a felt hood, made in the south for the crossing. It is too warm for a summer evening. Sten gave it away in one.

item_host_cup.name: The Host's Cup
item_host_cup.desc: A big ox-horn on a turned birch foot, banded in tin at the rim, from the high seat of Tarnhall. Every horn on the long table was full and frozen over. This one was dry, with a skin of dust inside it.

item_guest_tally.name: Guest-Tally
item_guest_tally.desc: A long plaited cord of yellow and oat wool, knotted once for each guest let in at the door. Lusse plaited it; the knots are the Host's, big and careful. Near the end the knots are all one knot, untied and tied again until the wool has felted.

goat_song.name: The Goat Song
goat_song.desc: A hall song about a goat that ate a sail, then the mast, then the man who said it couldn't. Thirty-one verses and one chorus. Lusse sings the verses. Anyone in earshot is the chorus, and she stops the song until they are.

item_ottar_staff.name: Ottar's Stick
item_ottar_staff.desc: A rowan walking stick with a horn cap, the bark left on for the grip. It was leaning inside the barred door, where you put a thing so you will see it on your way out. The mud on the tip is from the steps coming up.

item_barrel_head.name: Fish-Barrel Head
item_barrel_head.desc: The round pine head of a fish barrel, branded with a trader's mark: a knot inside a ring. Forty barrels came up the water for the feast. This one had only been started on; the nails are half drawn.

item_song_cord.name: Linnet's Song-cord
item_song_cord.desc: A knotted cord of plaited oat and yellow wool with a bone toggle, the knots of all sizes. It is an Outsong, tied by the one it was for, the night before she needed it. The last knot is left loose.

item_birch_ring.name: Ring of Plaited Birch
item_birch_ring.desc: A ring of birch bark plaited round on itself, small enough for one finger. It was in the ash at the foot of the eastmost clamp, where it would have been taken off to work. Eyvind plaited it in an evening and spent a week saying it was nothing.

item_knucklebone.name: Knucklebone
item_knucklebone.desc: A sheep's knucklebone, worn smooth. It was in the middle of the drove-road, on the side going east. There is a tooth-mark on it.

item_wool_ends.name: Ends of Wool
item_wool_ends.desc: Short ends of plaited wool, oat and yellow, cut with a billhook and swept into the corner of a collier's hut. A song-cord takes an evening to tie if you know what you want said. There are a great many ends here.

item_gate_latch.name: Gate Latch
item_gate_latch.desc: A latch and its keeper whittled from holly, oiled and never fitted. They were on the east post of a field with gateposts on two sides. The latch is cut to close from the left, and the keeper is cut for the right.

armour_collier.name: Collier's Leathers
armour_collier.desc: A soot-black leather apron and jerkin over oat wool, scorched at the hems, for working the clamps. The leather is cracked at the elbows. It smells of smoke whatever you do to it.

item_fold_tally.name: Fold-Tally
item_fold_tally.desc: A hazel stick notched down one edge: forty-three notches, one for every ewe put to the fell. Under them is one more, cut smaller, by a hand thirty years younger. Calder ran his thumb down it every night, and the small one is worn smooth.

item_calder_boots.name: Calder's Boots
item_calder_boots.desc: A pair of herd's boots, resoled more than once, the left heel worn down on the outside. They stood by the sheiling door with the toes to the wall, and the door was on the latch. They are dry inside.

item_shepherd_whistle.name: Shepherd's Whistle
item_shepherd_whistle.desc: A whistle cut from a ewe's shin-bone, two holes, for working a dog at distance. Calder made it for Sigga when she was eight. She learned to call instead, and the lanyard is still tied for a child's neck.

armour_fleece.name: Shepherd's Fleece
armour_fleece.desc: A coat of two fleeces sewn skin-side in, the wool left long, belted with rope. It turns sleet, and mostly it turns a tup's horn. One pocket is full of crumbled oatcake, kept for a ewe called Smudge.

armour_hall.name: Hall-Guard's Coat
armour_hall.desc: A quilted felt coat over a black mail shirt, yellow at the cuffs, with a fur cape for the draught at the doors. It hung on a peg inside the hall doors, by the bar. Whoever had the door that night took it off when the hall got hot, and stood his watch in his shirt.

item_latch_wool.name: Scrap of Woad Wool
item_latch_wool.desc: A scrap of woad-blue wool, pulled long, caught on the latch of the hall door at the height of a woman's hand. It is on the outside of the door. The bar was on the inside.

item_wren_band.name: Wren's Band
item_wren_band.desc: A mask-band of woad-blue wool, the nap worn off where it sat on wood. It was tied round the swaddle with a household knot, pulled tight with the teeth. It is far too long for what it went round, and was wrapped three times.

item_maren_mask.name: Maren's Mask
item_maren_mask.desc: A mourning mask of pale birch, smooth, the brow cut the Saltfell way. The band is gone and the wood is darker where it sat. A mask is carved for one burial and burned on the hearth before morning. This one is fifteen winters old.
